prune.description: destroy this scene's previously-applied actors that are no longer in the spec (tag-scoped; never touches hand-placed actors)

spec_json.description: the spec as inline JSON text (alternative to spec_path)

spec_path.description: path to a unreal.scene/v1 JSON spec file

tools.name: scene_apply

tools.description: Remove all actors a given scene_id previously applied (tag-scoped; leaves hand-placed actors untouched).

scene_id.description: the scene id whose actors to remove

tools.name: scene_clear

tools.description: Render a target (or the whole level) from N orbit angles into one contact-sheet montage — a quick multi-angle visual of a level/asset for design validation. Editor world (backgrounded-safe).

elevation.description: camera elevation degrees above horizon; default 25 (0 = horizontal orbit)

fill.description: fraction of the frame the target fills; default 0.7

fov.description: vertical field of view degrees; default 60

target.description: actor labels/globs to frame; empty = whole level

tools.name: scene_contact_sheet

tools.description: Deterministic quantize+SHA1 hash over actor OR HISM/ISM instance transforms — the authored-content oracle (verify a map hashes to an expected value; instance-aware where level_diff is not).

limit.description: instances scope: max instances to hash; default 5,000,000 (raise for a huge HISM city)

pos_bucket.description: position quantization in world units; default 1

tools.name: scene_digest

tools.description: Compile a scene spec and diff it against the current level (add/update/prune, missing asset refs) WITHOUT mutating — a dry run to review before scene_apply.
tools.name: scene_plan

tools.description: Reposition existing actors to their snapshot transforms (undo a move/rotate/scale experiment). Transform-only: it does NOT recreate actors deleted since the snapshot or remove ones spawned since (delete those with delete_actor / pie_destroy). Reports labels no longer present.
tools.name: scene_restore

tools.description: Save the current level's actor transforms (by label) to a named snapshot file so a MOVE/rotate/scale experiment can be undone with scene_restore. Scope is transforms only — it does not record spawns/deletes.

class_filter.description: only snapshot actors matching this class/label substring

tools.name: scene_snapshot

tools.description: Capture the actual display as a PNG — the whole virtual desktop (all monitors), one monitor, or a region. This is an OS screenshot of what is really on screen (unlike take_screenshot, which renders the 3D scene inside the editor). Downscaled to max_width for token economy.

max_width.description: downscale so the image is at most this many px wide (aspect preserved); default 1600, 0 = full resolution

monitor.description: monitor index (0-based, see list from MonitorRects); omit or -1 = whole virtual desktop spanning all monitors

region.description: [x,y,w,h] in virtual-desktop pixels to grab a sub-rectangle instead of a whole monitor

tools.name: screen_capture

tools.description: Start a play-in-editor session in the current level. simulate=true runs the world without possessing a player.

simulate.description: run the world without possessing a player pawn

tools.name: start_play

tools.description: Stop the current play-in-editor session.
tools.name: stop_play

tools.description: Run the style cohesion Layer-A deterministic audit (readonly) against captured frame paths.
tools.name: style_cohesion

tools.description: Render the scene and return it as a PNG image. Uses a synchronous scene capture so it works even when the editor is backgrounded (editor world only, not during PIE).
tools.name: take_screenshot

tools.description: Type a literal Unicode string at the OS level into the focused control (KEYEVENTF_UNICODE — layout-independent). Use for search boxes, names, and paths; use key_press for shortcuts and navigation keys.

text.description: the literal text to type as Unicode characters

tools.name: type_text

tools.description: Run the verb response Layer-A deterministic audit (readonly) against an input burst and envelope.
tools.name: verb_response

tools.description:
The editor viewport camera and selection (UI state; nothing is saved).
- op=get: camera {location, rotation} + game_view.
- op=set: location/rotation, pilot (actor) or eject, game_view.
- op=focus: aim the camera at `actors` (default: the selection).
- op=select: select `actors` (mode replace|add|remove|none), frame=true to focus them.
- op=selection: the selected actors (label, path, class).
Console commands moved to the console tool.

actors.description: focus/select: actor labels or object paths (focus default: the current selection)

distance_scale.description: focus: multiplier on the framing distance (default 2)

game_view.description: set: Game View on/off (hides editor-only actors, like pressing G)

pilot.description: set: pilot this actor (label or object path) with the camera

pitch.description: focus: camera pitch in degrees (default -30, negative looks down)

rotation.description: set: camera [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees

tools.name: viewport
tools.title: Editor viewport

tools.description:
Author a WidgetBlueprint's tree declaratively (create the asset with asset_create kind=widget_blueprint).
- op=compose: apply `tree` — add/update/reorder nodes, slots, props — then compile; never deletes. Re-composing the same tree is a no-op (same digest).
- op=prune: like compose, but DELETES every node absent from `tree` and the names in `remove`.
- op=compile: compile + save; returns the digest (and ends a deferred patch).
Check the result with widget_query op=tree / op=render.

defer.description: compose mode=patch: apply without compiling until op=compile

mode.description: compose: full (default; converge the whole tree on the spec, never deleting) | patch (only the given nodes)

remove.description: prune: also remove these named nodes

tree.description: compose/prune: declarative node {name, class, slot?, props?, brush?, font?, is_variable?, children?[]}; every node named; class is a friendly name (TextBlock, ProgressBar, Image, Button, CanvasPanel, VerticalBox, Overlay, ...) or a /Script or /Game path

tools.name: widget_edit
tools.title: Author UMG widgets

tools.description:
Inspect UMG widgets without PIE.
- op=tree: a WidgetBlueprint's tree as JSON + digest (compare digests to verify an edit).
- op=describe: the authorable palette (no class) or a class's editable props and slot type.
- op=render: SEE a UserWidget class — offscreen PNG (needs the plugin's MCPAuthoring module; writes Saved/MCP/WidgetRenders).

class.description: describe: a widget class (omit for the whole palette); render: the UserWidget class, e.g. /Script/MyGame.HudWidget or /Game/UI/WBP_HUD.WBP_HUD_C

tools.name: widget_query
tools.title: Inspect UMG widgets

tools.description: Capture a specific on-screen window as a PNG — defaults to auto-detecting the Unreal Editor. Sees the FULL editor: menus, panels, the Content Browser, modal dialogs, the composited viewport with UI. method=print (default) works even when the window is backgrounded/occluded and does not steal focus; method=screen blits its on-screen rectangle. Returns the window's screen bounds so you can map image pixels to mouse_control coordinates.

focus.description: bring the window to the foreground before capturing

hwnd.description: target an exact window handle (from list_windows)

max_width.description: downscale to at most this width; default 1600, 0 = full resolution

method.description: auto|print|screen. print (default) renders the window even when backgrounded/occluded and never steals focus; screen blits its on-screen rectangle (window must be visible)

pid.description: target a specific process id instead of by title

title.description: window title substring (case-insensitive); omit to auto-detect the Unreal Editor

tools.name: window_capture

tools.description: Spatial verification in the game world (PIE): line_trace (is a shot/LOS clear?), sphere_overlap (what's near a point?), nav_path (can AI path A->B?), project_point (is a point on the navmesh?). Needs collision + a built navmesh.

world.description: auto|editor|game; default auto (game world in PIE)

tools.name: world_query
